q3.text:
Q3. Pointer actions

A Skipped or Failed reason that a different tool or a pack fixes ends with one secondary button that names the destination, such as 'Install script pack'.

Opening a tool keeps the files open and selects that tool in the rail. Installing a pack never retries automatically: the files stay in the list for a new run.

Retry appears only after a wrong password, a timeout or a processing error.

save.text:
Save step

Tools that combine many files into one always open the native save dialog. Toolbox draws no dialog of its own, so the sheet on the Merge board is a placeholder for the system one. It proposes 'lease-agreement-merged.pdf' in the output location.

If the chosen name already exists, Toolbox writes 'lease-agreement-merged-1.pdf' instead, and the result row says so: 'Renamed to avoid replacing lease-agreement-merged.pdf'.

row4.text: PDF Editor: one document, like a viewer

editor.text:
PDF Editor model

One document per window, like Preview or Acrobat. Page thumbnails sit on the left, the page in the middle, and the inspector for the chosen tool on the right.

The edit toolbar is always visible: Organize, Crop, Edit text, Add text, Sign, Fill forms, Marks, Redact, plus More for Flatten, Split, Merge, Bates, Details and opening the Files view.

Edits are a list of changes that you can undo. The original file is never changed. Export a copy writes a new file and is disabled until something changes.

edkeys.text:
PDF Editor keyboard and screen reader

F6 cycles between the toolbar, thumbnails, page and inspector. The toolbar and thumbnail strip use arrow keys, with Home and End.

Every mark on the page is a focusable object with a name, such as 'Text box, Signed on 12 October, page 3'. Arrow keys nudge it, Shift+arrow moves it further, and Delete removes it.

Undo and Redo announce what they changed, such as 'Undid Add text'.

export.text:
Export order and redaction

Export applies changes in a fixed order: fill forms, edit text, overlays, flatten, then redact.

Before a redacted export, the disclosure says what happens. Affected pages become 300 dpi images. Metadata, XMP and attachments are removed. Annotations, form fields and layers on those pages are removed.

A signature is typed or an uploaded picture. It is not a digital signature, and the Sign panel says so.

conv.text:
One file from many

Images to PDF, Merge, Create GIF, App Icon Set, combining a TIFF and Formatted PDF all make one output. Their run button ends in an ellipsis and opens the native save dialog.

Tools that make one file per input use 'Save to' with an example name. A clash gets -1, -2 and so on, and errors stay per file.

row10.text: Settings, packs, shortcuts and the app icon

set.text:
Settings

Settings opens with Cmd/Ctrl+, from anywhere and replaces the tool rail with its sections. Changes save immediately; there is no Save button.

Switches are real switches with labels. Every section is reachable with Tab and arrow keys.

Packs never download without asking. A tool that needs a missing pack names it and its size, then sends you to this screen or installs it in place.

sec1.text:
Lock & Unlock: mode and passwords

The view is File Security and its one tool is Lock & Unlock, so the rail never reads File Security twice. Unlock also removes restrictions from PDFs that open without a password, with no password needed, and saves an unlocked copy.

Lock and Unlock is a segmented control in the header. Switching keeps the file list, clears both password fields and re-checks every row for the new mode. It is disabled while a batch runs.

The batch password sits at the top of the options with show/hide. Lock adds Confirm under it. A mismatch marks Confirm as invalid with 'Passwords don't match. Type the new password again.' and Run names the reason.

A row's own password opens an inline editor in that row, with Confirm in Lock. Saved rows show 'Own password' with Change and Use batch password. Clearing it shows a status line with Undo.

sec2.text:
Lock & Unlock: intake, flags and results

Files the other mode accepts stay in the list, flagged with a reason and a Won't run tag, such as a .doc in Lock. A banner offers one action to remove every flagged file. Files no mode accepts go under 'N items not added'.

Results use the shared row pattern. Locked or unlocked rows open or show the copy. A warning row says what changed, such as a removed signature or a -1 rename. Skipped rows say why and point to the fix, such as Unlock it first. Failed rows say why and whether the file is fine.

Retry appears only for a wrong password (Try another password, with an inline field) or a processing error. It runs only that file. A missing PDF helper fails PDFs only, and Office files still run.

Show all in Finder or File Explorer opens the destination once for many results.

sec3.text:
Lock & Unlock: local, destination, search

A note in the options says the tool runs on this device with no network, and that passwords are never saved and are cleared on a mode switch or on leaving. Results repeat that passwords were cleared.

Save to defaults to next to each original. Change for this run shows This run only and Reset to default. Copies end in -protected or -unlocked, and nothing is replaced.

Command center: File Security, lock icon. Find a tool matches lock, unlock, protect, password, encrypt and decrypt.

New patterns: the mode segmented control, inline row editors, and flagged rows with a Won't run tag.

row1.text: Finding a tool, adding files, choosing where outputs go

row2.text: Running a batch and reading the results

q8.text:
Q8. Six views and rail scaling

The command center lists the six views as sections with their tools inline. Any tool is one click away, and search is focused with Cmd/Ctrl+K.

Inside a view, the app sidebar becomes that view's tool rail. It's a plain vertical list that scrolls, so 12 or more tools fit without truncation. Short names come from the registry.

Below 980 px the rail turns into a horizontal strip under the header. Tools that don't fit go into a More menu. Arrow keys, Home and End work in both layouts.

q5.text:
Q5. Intake

With no files, the whole center pane is the drop target. Its border becomes solid and its text reads 'Drop to add' while files are dragged over it. Open files is the primary button, with the shortcut beside it. The accepted types are listed under it.

Files that aren't added are collected in a 'Not added' group under the list, each with its reason. A folder, a duplicate and a wrong type each get their own line. A wrong type can point to the right tool. Nothing in this group blocks the run.

q1.text:
Q1. Destination and per-run marking

'Save to' sits in the options panel, just above the Run button, and is always visible. The default reads 'Next to each original' or names the folder.

Change for this run opens the native folder dialog. The changed line gets a 'This run only' badge and a Reset to default link. Leaving the view clears it.

If the folder is missing or can't be written, a dialog appears before anything runs. It offers 'Choose another folder' or 'Save next to originals'. An example output name sits beside the destination line.

q4.text:
Q4. Passwords and overrides

One masked field covers the whole batch. It has a show/hide eye and the note 'Never saved'.

A file with its own password shows a key badge, 'Own password', in the list's Password column. Every other file reads 'Batch password'. The override is set from the row's menu.

After a wrong password, the failed row opens an inline password field and Retry, so only that file runs again.

q7.text:
Q7. Shortcut hints

Hints appear only on the control they trigger, as a small key cap inside the button:
- Open files: Cmd/Ctrl+O
- Run: Cmd/Ctrl+Enter
- Find a tool: Cmd/Ctrl+K
- Settings: Cmd/Ctrl+,
- Cancel: Esc

List hints (Delete removes, Shift or Cmd/Ctrl-click selects) appear as one quiet line above the list once files are added.

All labels switch between Cmd and Ctrl, and between Finder and File Explorer, by platform. Use the Platform tweak on any screen to see both.

q6.text:
Q6. Progress, cancel, locked state

The batch strip at the top of the list shows 'Protecting 7 of 24'. Its bar fills one segment per finished file, coloured by result. Rows switch from Waiting to a spinner to their result as each file finishes, and finished outputs can be opened right away.

The options panel dims, with one line: 'Options are locked until the batch finishes'. The Run button becomes 'Cancel batch' (Esc).

Cancel asks first, saying what is kept and what won't run. Cancelled files become Skipped, with the reason 'Cancelled'.

q2.text:
Q2. Three-state rows and large batches

Each row has an icon, a word and a reason, so the state never depends on colour:
- Succeeded: a check.
- Skipped: a grey dash. It's a no-op, not a problem.
- Failed: a red cross.
Warnings are amber and sit under the output name.

The summary counts double as filters. In large batches, 'Needs attention' groups rows by reason, so 28 'Signature removed' rows become one group you can expand. The list keeps input order.

sr.text:
Screen-reader announcements

One polite live region sits on the batch strip:
- On start: 'Protecting 24 files.'
- During the run: progress every 5 files or 10 seconds, whichever is later, such as 'Protecting, 10 of 24 done.'
- On finish: 'Done. 21 protected, 2 skipped, 1 failed.' Focus stays where it was.

Each row is a list item whose accessible name reads as one sentence: file, state, reason, warnings, then output name. Row actions are real buttons, such as 'Open annual-report-protected.pdf'.

The cancel dialog traps focus and returns it to Cancel batch.

ep1.text:
Edit PDF Q1. Grouping: overlays vs document operations

The toolbar groups tools by what they do, split by separators: page operations (Organize, Crop), content edits (Edit text, Add text, Sign, Fill form), range overlays (Watermark, Page numbers, Header and footer), then Redact. More holds Flatten, Split, Merge, Bates and Details.

Overlays put a selectable object on the page. It has a blue outline and the inspector edits it, ending with a Remove action such as 'Remove watermark'. Document operations change pages, so they open their own view (Organize) or act on the whole file. They show no object on the page.

The inspector title always names the active tool.

ep2.text:
Edit PDF Q2. Export summary, fixed order, disabled Export

PdfExport Review lists every contributing change under 'Changes, applied in this fixed order': forms, edit text, overlays, flatten, then redact. Each row names the tool and its pages.

Nothing to export: Export in the header is disabled, and a tooltip explains why: nothing has changed yet, and the run shortcut does nothing.

Export blocked: the Export button is disabled with aria-describedby pointing at the reason, a missing Devanagari script pack. The reason sits directly above the button, with the fix (Install script pack, 38 MB) inside it.

While exporting, the document is locked and the background is aria-hidden. Cancel export (Esc) is the only action.

ep3.text:
Edit PDF Q3. Destination and per-run change

The empty PdfOpen view says copies save next to the original and that another folder can be picked at export.

In the Export dialog, Save to shows the folder. The default is 'Same folder as the original.' PdfExport Other folder shows a changed folder with a 'This export only' badge, a 'Reset to default' button and the hint 'Next export goes back to the original's folder.'

Bates shows the same pattern in its destination bar: 'This run only' and Reset to default. Its empty state shows the default, the same folder as each original. It follows the shared Q1 rule on the Destination board.

ep4.text:
Edit PDF Q4. Form fields, Tab order, required and invalid

Fields show as tinted boxes on the page. The focused field has a blue ring. Required fields have a red asterisk in the label, and the inspector's Fields list shows 'Required, empty'. 'Go to next empty required field' jumps to the next one.

PdfForms Tab order: numbered blue badges 1 to 8 sit beside each field, in the order Tab follows. The checkbox 'Show Tab order on the page' turns them on. Tab order comes from the PDF and is shown, not edited.

PdfForms Invalid entry: the field gets a red border, aria-invalid, and an inline reason ('Not a real date') tied by aria-describedby. The Fields list, the summary and the status line name it too.

ep5.text:
Edit PDF Q5. Typed signature, reuse, reminder

PdfSign Placing: in the typed mode, the name shows in the chosen signature style before you place it. The picture mode uses an image file instead. Either way, you click the page to place it.

PdfSign Use again: signatures already used are listed with a preview. Picking one and clicking the page places it again. 'Placed so far' lists each copy, and each copy can be moved, resized or deleted on its own. New signature and Clear list are below.

The reminder stays visible under the intro in both panels: this is a picture of a signature, not a digital signature. The reuse list points to it with aria-describedby.

ep6.text:
Edit PDF Q6. Range-applied objects

Watermark, page numbers and header and footer are each one object that applies to a page range.

A chip above the page (for example 'Pages 1–14') says which range it covers, with the line 'One watermark, applied to every page in the range. Edit it once, on any page.' Selecting it on any page selects the same object, and every change shows on all pages in the range.

The Pages section in the inspector sets the range: All, Skip the first page, or These pages. The status line confirms how many pages it covers.

ep7.text:
Edit PDF Q7. Token insertion

Header and footer has six labelled boxes: Left, Centre and Right for the header and for the footer. Insert buttons (Page number, Page count, Date, File name) add a token into the box last selected.

Tokens show as blue tags inside the box. They are not typed codes such as {date}, so nobody has to learn a syntax. Backspace removes a whole tag. The page preview shows the filled-in values, such as '3 of 14'.

Bates Stamp text uses the same tag box and Insert buttons: Bates number, File name, Page in file, Date. Stamp text must contain the Bates number.

ep8.text:
Edit PDF Q8. Redaction: mark, search, review, disclosure

Marking: drag over anything to remove. Marks are previews until export, are listed in the inspector, and can be resized or removed.

Search results: 'Find text to redact' lists each match with its page and context. Check the matches to mark, then use Mark selected.

Reviewing: 'Preview as exported' shows marks as solid black. Previous and Next step through every mark, with 'Mark 2 of 5' announced, and Remove drops one.

Export disclosure: a dialog shown before a redacted export. It says which pages become 300 dpi images and that their comments, form fields and hidden layers are removed. Metadata, XMP and attachments go too. Export needs 'I've checked the marks on every page' ticked.

ep9.text:
Edit PDF Q9. Flatten, result warnings, unavailable sub-tool

Flatten confirmation (PdfForms flatten Confirming): a dialog titled 'Flatten fields in the copy?' says what becomes permanent and names the required fields still empty. Its buttons are Keep fields editable and Flatten when exporting.

Result warnings (PdfExport Done with warnings): the copy is saved, and '2 things to check' lists 'Digital signature removed' and 'Font substituted on pages 1 and 3', each with what changed.

Unavailable sub-tool (PdfForms Unsupported form): an XFA form shows a warning in the inspector, explains why, and offers 'Use Add text instead'. Non-editable text (PdfEditText Not editable) offers OCR or Add text.

ep10.text:
Edit PDF Q10. Errors at open

Encrypted PDF (PdfOpen Locked file): the file isn't opened. Unlock in File Security makes an unlocked copy, and the original stays locked.

Limit exceeded (PdfOpen Too many pages): 'court-bundle.pdf is too large to edit' gives the page count and the limit. It offers Split into parts or another PDF. The 2,000-page limit is a placeholder until engineering measures the real ceiling.

Signed file: opens with a warning that exporting removes the digital signature, which the Done-with-warnings result repeats.

Skipped never happens in Edit PDF. It edits one document, so a no-op export is prevented by disabling Export (Nothing to export).

ep11.text:
Edit PDF Q11. Script-pack prompt

Typing text the bundled fonts can't draw (PdfText scriptPackPrompt) shows the text box with a warning in the inspector. The warning names the script and says the box can't be exported until the pack is installed. 'Install script pack' gives the download size and is installed once for all tools.

If you export anyway, PdfExport Export blocked repeats the same message and button above the disabled Export. The wording and the Install action match the optional-pack rows in #445 (Packs, PackResults), so the pack is named the same everywhere.

ep12.text:
Edit PDF Q12. Unexported-changes warning

Closing the window, opening another PDF or going back to All tools with changes that haven't been exported opens 'Export your changes before closing?' (PdfExport Closing with changes). It gives the number of changes and says they're lost on close.

The buttons are Discard changes, Cancel and Export….

The header subtitle keeps a running count, such as '1 change not exported', so the warning is never a surprise.

ep13.text:
Edit PDF Q13. Focus, screen reader, macOS and Windows

Dialogs trap focus and return it to the control that opened them. While a dialog is open, the background is aria-hidden.

Disabled actions point to their reason with aria-describedby: Export, Number files and Export blocked. Status lines are role=status and announce results, such as 'Mark 2 of 5', '3 numbered, 1 failed'.

Platform labels change with the platform property. ⌘ becomes Ctrl, ⌘↵ becomes Ctrl+Enter, ⇧⌘Z becomes Ctrl+Y, Show in Finder becomes Show in File Explorer, and paths use C:\Users\Asha\… with backslashes. Every board renders in both themes.

epb1.text:
Bates Q. File order, preview, ranges, unused gap

Files are listed in numbering order. Each row has a drag grip and Move up, Move down and Remove buttons, so it can be reordered by mouse or keyboard. The Numbers column previews each file's range before anything runs, and the inspector shows an example stamp on a page.

A locked file is flagged before the run. It is skipped and given no numbers, so the set has no gap (Done).

A file that fails during the run keeps the numbers set aside for it, because later files are already stamped. The row shows that range struck through with 'Unused gap', and the banner names it: 'HL000017 to HL000019 are unused.' Copy number list includes the gap.

epb2.text:
Bates Q. Empty, running, results

No files: a drop target with Add PDFs and its shortcut. Number files is disabled with the reason 'Add PDFs first', and the destination reads the same folder as each original.

Numbering: an overall progress bar and per-file progress ('Page 4 of 9'). Add PDFs, Change… and the options are locked. Cancel (Esc) replaces the Run button, and Skip stops just the current file.

Results: saved rows have Open and Show in Finder (Show in File Explorer on Windows), and the banner has Copy number list. This is the only multi-file sub-tool, so it uses a file list instead of the page canvas.

og1.text:
Organize: rail and page view

Organize is the first item in the PDF Editor rail and the place a PDF opens. It's a full-width page grid, not a strip beside the page. Every other rail item (Crop, Edit text, Sign…) shows one page at a time.

To switch: press Enter or double-click a thumbnail, or use "Open in page view" under the preview. That opens the focused page in the last page tool you used, Edit text by default. Choosing Organize in the rail comes back to the grid with the same focus and selection.

The right panel previews the focused page large, with its position, original page and orientation, so users can check a page without leaving the grid.

og2.text:
Thumbnails, drag and scrolling

Size: Small, Medium (default) or Large, a segmented control at the right of the Select bar. The choice is remembered for the app, not per file.

Each thumbnail shows its position in bold. A page that moved adds "· was page 13". The screen reader always hears both: "Position 12, original page 13".

Drag: dragging any selected page carries the whole selection. The pointer shows a small stack with a count badge (3). The pages being moved are dimmed in place. A blue bar with end caps shows where they'll land, always between two pages.

Auto-scroll: 44-pixel bands at the top and bottom of the grid. They appear only during a drag. Hovering a band scrolls that way, faster nearer the edge, and the band says what is coming into view. Esc cancels the drag and nothing moves.

og3.text:
Orientation

One segmented group in the page actions bar: rotate left, rotate right, mirror left to right, mirror top to bottom, plus a ▾ menu. The menu repeats those four with their shortcuts and adds Rotate 180° and "Reset orientation of N pages", which only undoes orientation.

The thumbnail itself turns and flips, so users see the result. A small badge in the bottom-left corner states it in words and symbols: "↻ 90°", "↺ 90°", "↻ 180°", "⇋ Mirrored", "⇵ Mirrored", joined with "·" when both apply. A page with no change has no badge.

The preview panel's Orientation line spells it out: "Rotated 90° right, mirrored left to right" or "As in the original".

og4.text:
Notices and preflight

Notices sit at the top of the grid, above the pages, as quiet rows with an icon and plain words. They never block the grid.

- Signed PDF: on open. "This PDF is digitally signed. Any copy you export won't be signed any more. The original keeps its signature." Dismissable with Got it. It returns as "Signature removed" in the export result.
- Mirrored pages: whenever any page is mirrored. "2 mirrored pages will show their text reversed. That's expected…"

Preflight rejections replace the grid with a centered message, an icon and the next step. No pages are shown and nothing is changed:
- Password-protected: Open File Security.
- Damaged or unsupported: Open another PDF.
- Over the page limit (2,000 is a placeholder until the spec fixes it): Open Split.

og5.text:
Selecting pages

The Select bar sits under the page actions: All, Odd, Even, Blank pages, None. "Blank pages" sits right after Odd and Even because it's the same kind of action: it only selects.

After it runs, the button keeps a "3 found" chip. The pages are selected and labelled "· blank" in the grid. Focus moves to the first one, and the status line says "3 blank pages found and selected: 7, 11 and 16. Nothing was removed." Users review them, deselect any they want to keep, then press Delete. Finding zero says "No blank pages found" and changes nothing. Selecting never adds an undo step.

The Pages field takes ranges like "1-3, 7" and selects them on Enter. It uses the same rules as Split. A page past the end is an error: red border and the message "Page 250 isn't in this PDF. It has 236 pages…".

The count is always visible at the left of the actions bar: "3 pages selected", or "No pages selected" with the actions disabled.

og6.text:
Moving, deleting and shortcuts

Move earlier and later go one step. "Move to…" opens a small popover with a position field and Start and End buttons. "Page order" holds Reverse the selected pages, Reverse the whole document and Interleave a two-sided scan, with a line explaining when to use it.

Delete names the count: "Delete 3 pages". With every page selected it's disabled, and an alert explains: "A PDF needs at least one page…".

Shortcuts: the keyboard button (or ?) opens the full list. The grid is one tab stop. Arrow keys, Home and End move focus. Space selects. Shift plus an arrow extends. ⌘/Ctrl plus an arrow moves the selection. ⌘↑/⌘↓ on Mac and Ctrl+Home/End on Windows move it to the start or end. M opens Move to. Rotate is ⌘R/Ctrl+R, and with Shift it rotates left. H and V mirror. Delete or ⌫ removes. Every Mac label has a Windows label.

og7.text:
Export, destination and results

Next to Export is a folder button with the destination's short name, by default the original's folder. Clicking it opens a popover with the full path, Choose folder… and Use default. A per-run change shows a "This export only" chip and says the Settings default didn't change.

Export is disabled until the previews are ready and while nothing has changed. Undoing back to the original disables it again, with "Nothing to export yet". This view never shows Skipped.

Running: Export becomes a progress bar with "Page 137 of 236" and Cancel. Page edits are locked, with a notice saying so.

Exported: a dialog with the file (contracts-scan-edited.pdf, then -edited-1), "233 pages kept, 3 removed, 12 rotated, 2 mirrored", the folder, and "Signature removed" when relevant. Buttons: Open, Show in Finder / Show in File Explorer, and Keep editing.

Failed: names the problem, the folder, and "Nothing. No partial file was left behind."

Removal blocked: lists what depends on the pages (bookmarks, form fields, tags), says nothing was saved, and offers to restore those pages.

og8.text:
Reset, unsaved changes, motion and screen readers

Reset… (header) asks first. It's an alert dialog that returns every page to how the PDF was opened, and says it also clears other PDF Editor changes. Opening another PDF with changes asks "Export your changes first?" with Export, Cancel and Don't export.

Reduced motion: reordering normally slides pages into place over 150 ms, and drops settle the same way. With reduced motion on, pages jump straight to their new place, the drag ghost has no tilt, and rotation applies without turning. Auto-scroll still works but moves in steps.

Screen readers: the grid is a multi-select listbox. Each option is "Position 12, original page 13, rotated 90° right, mirrored left to right, selected". The footer status is a polite live region. It says things like "Pages 4 to 6 moved to position 1", "Page 5 rotated 90° right", "Pages 8 and 9 mirrored left to right", "3 blank pages found and selected: 7, 11 and 16", "No blank pages found" and "3 pages deleted. 233 left." Errors, the last-page message and failed exports are alerts.

row12.text: Optional packs: Settings, tool prompts and results

pk1.text:
Packs: layout and disk use

Packs is a plain list in Settings, not cards, with one row per pack. The row shows the name, what uses it and its size. Status and actions sit on the right. Status is always words, with an icon or bar where it helps, never colour alone.

A chevron opens a row's details: what it does, which tools use it, download size, size on this disk, version and license. License text sits only in details, with View license.

The privacy statement is the first paragraph: one download from the Toolbox release server, checked before use, works offline, and your files never leave this device.

Install from file… sits beside the heading in every state. On a computer without internet it's the main way in.

Installed rows show their own size on this disk. The line under the list gives the total: "3 installed, 415 MB used. 48 GB free on this disk."

pk2.text:
Pack statuses and actions

- Not installed: "Not installed", with Install.
- Downloading: bar plus "7 of 12 MB", with Cancel.
- Checking: full bar plus "Checking the download…", with Cancel.
- Waiting: "Waiting. Starts after the downloads above.", with Cancel. Packs install one at a time.
- Installed: "Installed, version 2.0", with Remove…
- Update available: "Version 3.1. Update to 3.2, 12 MB", with Update and Remove…
- Updating: bar plus "Updating, 5 of 12 MB", with Cancel. The row says version 3.1 keeps working until 3.2 is ready. A cancelled or failed update keeps 3.1.
- Damaged: red text, with Repair and Remove…, plus a banner at the top.
- Doesn't work with this version: amber text, with Check for updates (opens Settings, Updates) and Remove…

Remove… asks first: "Remove Text recognition, Hindi? OCR can't read Hindi until you install it again. Frees 31 MB."

pk3.text:
Prompts inside tools

In a tool, the prompt is a note in the options panel, next to the setting that needs the pack. It names the pack and its download size and has one Install button. Examples: "Hindi needs a 12 MB download." in OCR, and the script note in the Edit PDF text inspector. The tool stays usable while it downloads.

On a result row, the prompt is one secondary button that names the action: Install Hindi pack, Update Gujarati pack or Repair Tamil pack. The row says "Needs a pack". It never offers Retry.

When the pack finishes installing, the row changes to "Ready to run" with a "Pack installed" badge. The status line says "Hindi pack installed. 2 files are ready to run again." The files stay in the list until the user runs again.

OCR language picker: two groups. "Installed" lists languages that are ready; ones already added are dimmed with "Added". "Download to use" lists the rest with a download icon and size. Choosing one adds it to the list as "Not installed" with the Install note.

pk4.text:
Final error copy

Offline: "You're offline. Installed packs keep working. Connect to the internet to install or update packs, or use Install from file." Row: "No internet connection." Install is disabled.

Blocked server: "Couldn't reach the Toolbox release server. Your internet works, but something on this network is blocking downloads from Toolbox. Try again later or on another network, or install from a pack file."

Interrupted: "Download stopped before it finished. Nothing was installed." with Try again, which starts over.

Not enough space: "Not enough space for Office documents. It needs 310 MB free and this disk has 120 MB. Free up at least 190 MB, then try again."

Check failed (download): "The download didn't pass its safety check, so it was deleted. Nothing was installed."

Wrong computer (file): "This pack file is for another kind of computer. It was made for a Mac, so it can't be installed here. Nothing was installed. Get the pack file for Windows on this processor from the Toolbox releases page."

Not signed (file): "This file isn't a Toolbox pack. It isn't signed by Toolbox, so it can't be installed. Nothing was installed."

Check failed (file): "This pack file didn't pass its safety check. It may be damaged or changed since it was made, so it was not installed."

In use: "Text recognition, English wasn't removed. OCR is using it right now. Remove it after the run finishes."

pk5.text:
Packs keyboard and screen reader

Settings, Packs: Tab goes to Install from file…, then each row in order. Within a row, Tab goes to the details chevron, then the row's actions from left to right. Enter or Space opens and closes details. Details content is read in order and isn't a stop.

Names for tests:
- The list is "Packs". Each row is "<pack name>, <status>".
- The chevron is "Details for <pack name>" with aria-expanded.
- Buttons are "<action> <pack name>", such as "Install Text recognition, Hindi" and "Cancel Text recognition, Hindi".
- Progress bars are "Downloading <pack name>", "Checking <pack name>" or "Updating <pack name>".
- Status text is a polite live region. Damaged, in use and server errors are alerts.

Install from file: the native open dialog, then a dialog called "Install this pack?" with Cancel first and Install as the default. Rejection dialogs are alert dialogs with "Choose another file…" and OK.

OCR picker: a combobox "Add a language" that opens a listbox with the groups "Installed" and "Download to use". Options are named "<language>, installed" or "<language>, not installed, <size> download". Arrow keys move, Enter chooses and Escape closes.

Result rows: the action is "<action> for <file name>", such as "Install Hindi pack for ration-card-hindi.pdf".
